precepts.text: Go to Shiloh and see what I did to it; I will cast out Judah as I cast out the whole seed of Ephraim.
precepts.point: Amaziah, priest of Bethel, told Amos to go prophesy in Judah and not in the king's chapel. Amos was sent to his own people, as God always sends prophets to Israel alone.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Amos warns Ephraim, “seek not Beth–el, nor enter into Gilgal”, for “Beth–el shall come to nought.” These were places built for worship by Abraham and Jacob, and Ephraim turned them into seats of idolatry. So Gilgal would surely go into captivity, and Beth–el would be destroyed. “Seek the Lord, and ye shall live; lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph”: the house of Joseph is Ephraim.

Jeremiah turns the same judgment on Judah: “But go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.” Go look at Shiloh and see what I did to it. “I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking, but ye heard not; and I called you, but ye answered not”: they refused the prophets.

“Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name, wherein ye trust, and unto the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh. And I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.” What was done to Ephraim will be done to Judah: the heathen come in, destroy the sanctuary and lead them captive. The exact same way. The same thing happens to both houses, both kingdoms. He raised up Assyria to overthrow Ephraim, and he raised up Babylon to overthrow Judah.

And they would not hear it. Amaziah the priest of Bethel, one of the low-level priests raised up that was not Levi, told Amos, “go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel”. Go teach Judah; you are disturbing the king's church. Amos was blitzing the churches. But the Lord said to him, “Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.” The Lord always sent his prophets to his people, and his people alone, to repent. It is the same with Jacob today: the one preaching the word of God is called a troublemaker.

So Bethel came to nought as Shiloh did, and Israel went “into captivity forth of his land”: their wives made harlots, their sons and daughters fallen by the sword, their land divided by line as it is to this day, dying “in a polluted land”. That began with the northern kingdom, but eventually it happened to all of us as a whole.

precepts.text: Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices; I commanded not burnt offerings, but this thing: obey my voice, and I will be your God.
precepts.point: Israel took the nourishment of the Lord for granted, and he grew tired of the empty offerings: put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. He spake not unto our fathers concerning burnt offerings, but this thing commanded he: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people. He never wanted the sacrifices above obedience; today he does not want an apology or money in the plate, he wants you to obey his voice and repent.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
The offerings were the collateral of those times, scaled to what a man could bring, and families felt the after-effects of always sacrificing: the livestock and the agriculture went for your sins, and the household lacked because of it. Israel took the nourishment of the Lord for granted, and He grew tired of the empty offerings.

“Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.”

He never wanted the sacrifices above obedience. Today He does not want an apology or money in the plate; He wants you to obey His voice and repent.

precepts.text: Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices; I commanded obedience: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people.
precepts.point: Jeremiah carries the same word: I spake not unto your fathers concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices, but this thing commanded I them, obey my voice. Yet they hearkened not, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart and went backward and not forward; speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken. That is seen every sabbath on the streets.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
Jeremiah carries the same word as Hosea: “Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.”

Yet they hearkened not, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart and went backward and not forward; speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken. That is seen every sabbath on the streets.

precepts.text: I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: but this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people.
precepts.point: Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord; not the blood of bulls and of goats, but mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments. The sacrifices were added because of transgression, the animal's blood taken in your place so the Most High would not have to kill you; you read of it from Genesis 3, where the Lord took the skins after Adam sinned. Yet there were some things you could not sacrifice for, abominations for which a man's own blood was required.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.”

Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord. What he commanded first was obedience: mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments. The sacrifices were added because of transgression.

precepts.text: Because they built the high places of Topheth to burn their sons and daughters, the Lord said it would be called the valley of slaughter and their carcases would be meat for the fowls.
precepts.point: Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children, and it had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
The Lord says, “they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart.”

Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children. It had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own, and Josiah “defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.”

And the Lord said what it would become: “it shall no more be called Tophet, nor the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter: for they shall bury in Tophet, till there be no place. And the carcases of this people shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth.”

precepts.text: They built the high places of Tophet in the valley of Hinnom to burn their sons and daughters in the fire, a thing the Most High commanded not, neither came it into His heart.
precepts.point: He burned incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom and burned his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen that the Most High cast out before the children of Israel. This was witchcraft and child sacrifice, the practice called Tophet, in the high places under every green tree.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

precepts.why:
“For the children of Judah have done evil in my sight, saith the Lord”. “And they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart.”

That is what Ahaz did. He “burnt incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burnt his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen whom the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel.” This was witchcraft and child sacrifice, the practice called Tophet, in the high places “and under every green tree.”

Ahaz “did not that which was right in the sight of the Lord, like David his father”. He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and “made also molten images for Baalim”, a thing the Most High commanded not, neither came it into his heart.

precepts.text: The Most High spake not to the fathers concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices when He brought them out of Egypt.
precepts.point: Christ did only what the Most High intended, to make His soul an offering for sin. The scripture always shows that sacrifice was temporary and that obedience and mercy were desired above it.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
The Most High said, “I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices”. Sacrifice was never the heart of what he asked of Israel when he brought them out of Egypt.

That is why setting aside the sacrifice and offerings is not changing the customs Moses delivered, as the false witnesses claimed. The scripture always shows that sacrifice was temporary. It is written throughout the old testament, so Christ destroyed nothing of the law when the sacrifice was set aside.
